entries.title: Down, distance and field position
entries.summary: Offensive and defensive decisions are constrained by down, yards-to-gain, field position, clock and score; tendencies must be conditioned on situation.
principles: Avoid treating aggregate tendencies as situation-free.
Separate neutral situations from obvious passing/rushing situations.
fantasyImplications: Usage and efficiency expectations should account for likely game situations, but fantasy weighting requires validation.

entries.title: Offensive personnel groupings
entries.summary: Personnel groupings describe eligible skill-position composition and shape the defensive response, formation possibilities and player opportunity.
principles: Track RB/TE/WR composition separately from formation.
Personnel and alignment are related but not identical.
limitations: Teams can create atypical formations from the same personnel.
fantasyImplications: Personnel participation can clarify route/touch opportunity and role stability.

entries.title: X, Z and slot receiver roles
entries.summary: Receiver labels describe alignment and assignment tendencies, not fixed player archetypes. X is commonly attached to the line, Z commonly aligns off the line and can motion more freely, while slot describes an inside alignment; modern offenses move players among roles.
principles: Separate listed position from snap alignment.
limitations: Terminology varies by system and modern offenses blur traditional labels.
fantasyImplications: Alignment and motion can change matchup, release access, route tree and target opportunity.

provenance.note: Played Z/slot in a motion-heavy offense; frequent pre-snap motion used to read defensive response.

entries.title: Run concept families
entries.summary: Run games can be organized into broad zone and gap/man families, with concepts such as inside/outside zone, power, counter, duo and related variants creating different blocking rules and reads.
principles: Identify concept family before attributing RB performance solely to player talent.
Consider box count, front, line movement and back read.
limitations: Terminology and blocking details vary by team.
fantasyImplications: Scheme fit, line health and defensive front interaction may affect rushing opportunity/efficiency; predictive use requires validation.

entries.title: Pass protection structure
entries.summary: Protection rules determine how an offense accounts for rushers and influence route participation, quarterback timing and pressure responses.
principles: Account for RB/TE protection responsibilities when evaluating receiving opportunity.
limitations: Protection calls and adjustments are often not fully observable from public data.
fantasyImplications: Protection burden can alter routes and targets for RB/TE and change QB/WR efficiency.
